test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which of the following has been emphasized for the first time in criminal law regarding sexual offences?

options.text: Marital rape as a punishable offense
Consent must be explicitly defined and recorded
Death penalty for all rape cases
Gender neutrality in sexual assault definitions

solution:
The correct answer is __**Gender neutrality in sexual assault definitions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**, which replaced the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** of **1860**, has introduced a significant shift by emphasizing **gender neutrality** in several definitions related to sexual assault and victims. While the core definition of rape under **Section 63** remains largely gender-specific (perpetrated by a man), the BNS 2023 moves toward recognizing **transgender persons** and uses more inclusive language in various sections related to sexual offenses. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• One of the most notable additions is **Section 69**, which specifically criminalizes sexual intercourse through **deceitful means** or a **false promise to marry**. This is the first time such an offense has been codified with a distinct punishment of up to **10 years** of **imprisonment**, moving away from the previous ambiguity in the **IPC**.
 
• The **BNS 2023** prioritizes offenses against **women and children** by placing them in **Chapter 5** of the code. This structural change signifies the legislature's intent to give paramount importance to these crimes compared to the **IPC**, where such offenses were placed much later in the document.
 
• Regarding **marital rape**, the **BNS 2023** retains the **exception** (Exception 2 to Section 63) which states that sexual intercourse by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under **18 years** of age, is not rape. Therefore, marital rape has not been made a punishable offense under this new Sanhita. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• While the **death penalty** is a possible punishment under **Section 70(2)** for the **gang rape** of a girl under **18 years** of age, it is not prescribed for "all" rape cases. The law maintains a hierarchy of punishments based on the severity and age of the victim. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Implementation and Timeline:** The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)** received the assent of the **President of India** on **December 25, 2023**. It officially came into force on **July 1, 2024**, marking a new era in the Indian criminal justice system by repealing the **British-era IPC**.
 
• **Definition of Consent:** Under the **BNS**, **consent** is defined as an unequivocal voluntary agreement when the woman by words, gestures, or any form of verbal or non-verbal communication, communicates willingness to participate in the specific sexual act. However, this definition was already evolved through the **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013**; thus, it is not a "first time" inclusion in **2023**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Aggravated Punishment:** The **BNS 2023** increases the minimum punishment for **rape** from **7 years** to **10 years** of **rigorous imprisonment**. For the **gang rape** of a woman, the punishment is **imprisonment for life** (which means the remainder of that person's natural life) or **rigorous imprisonment** for a term not less than **20 years**.
 
• **Protection of Minors:** The new code emphasizes the protection of **children** (defined as anyone under **18 years**). Crimes against children carry much more stringent penalties, including the **death penalty** or **life imprisonment** without the possibility of remission in specific aggravated cases.
 
• **Community Service:** For the first time in Indian criminal law, the **BNS 2023** introduces **Community Service** as a form of **punishment** for petty offenses, aiming at a more **reformative** approach to justice rather than purely **retributive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 63 (Rape):** Replaces **Section 375** of the **IPC**. It maintains the **four-step** definition of the act but adds clarity to the **punitive measures** in subsequent sections.
 
• **Section 70 (Gang Rape):** Specifically deals with **gang rape**, providing a minimum of **20 years** of imprisonment or **life imprisonment**.
 
• **Rights of the Victim:** The **BNS**, alongside the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, emphasizes that the **victim’s statement** must be recorded through **audio-video means** in sexual offense cases to ensure transparency and prevent tampering.
 
• **Deceitful Means (Section 69):** This includes the use of **false promises** regarding **employment**, **promotion**, or **marriage** while concealing one's **identity**. It addresses a long-standing gap where such cases were previously litigated under general rape or cheating provisions.
